result.finding: Assessed 6 CWE rules in Concurrency & Synchronization: 0 FOUND, 6 NOT_FOUND
evidence: Scanned first-party production C# source, Razor pages, JavaScript, CSS, application and project configuration, Dockerfile, Azure deployment configuration, Bicep infrastructure, deployment hooks, provisioning scripts, and SQL configuration scripts. Excluded tests, generated code/artifacts, third-party libraries, and development-agent tooling; never read .github/agents.

PhotoAlbum/Program.cs:22-26 registers PhotoAlbumContext with default scoped lifetime and PhotoService explicitly as scoped; request handlers neither share these instances across requests nor invoke their operations concurrently.

PhotoAlbum/Services/PhotoService.cs:22-23 initializes the application-owned static collection during CLR type initialization; its only subsequent access is Contains at line 134, with no mutation or exposure.

PhotoAlbum/Pages/Index.cshtml.cs:60-94 uses request-local collections and sequential awaits. PhotoAlbum/Services/PhotoService.cs:144-159 uses fresh GUID filenames and operation-local streams disposed before database metadata publication.

No concrete reachable unsafe shared mutable memory, application-defined singleton initialization, parallel task fan-out, background workers, custom locking, or synchronization mechanism was identified. Browser code has no workers or shared memory.

Reviewed deletion, retrieval, compensation, and startup migration paths. EF optimistic database deletion conflicts, multi-resource compensation, and file disappearance during retrieval do not establish multithreaded shared-memory synchronization vulnerabilities.

values.name: Use of Singleton Pattern Without Synchronization in a Multithreaded Context
values.description: The product uses the singleton pattern when creating a resource within a multithreaded environment.

values.name: Unsynchronized Access to Shared Data in a Multithreaded Context
values.description: The product does not properly synchronize shared data, such as static variables across threads, which can lead to undefined behavior and unpredictable data changes.

values.name: Improper Synchronization
values.description: The product utilizes multiple threads or processes to allow temporary access to a shared resource that can only be exclusive to one process at a time, but it does not properly synchronize these actions, which might cause simultaneous accesses of this resource by multiple threads or processes.

values.name: Improper Locking
values.description: The product does not properly acquire or release a lock on a resource, leading to unexpected resource state changes and behaviors.

values.name: Missing Synchronization
values.description: The product utilizes a shared resource in a concurrent manner but does not attempt to synchronize access to the resource.

values.name: Incorrect Synchronization
values.description: The product utilizes a shared resource in a concurrent manner, but it does not correctly synchronize access to the resource.
